turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he was grateful for all she had done for him and that he would take good care of himself and bring honor to the family, just as she had always taught him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would take care of everything, that he would make sure their son was well-fed and well-educated, and that he would honor her memory by doing so.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked if there was anything she could do to help, her voice barely above a whisper, as she hovered near her mother-in-law's bedside, her eyes cast downward.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung and the eldest son, her eyes filled with a deep sadness, and told Wang Lung that it was not the son's education or food that she was worried about, but that he find a good wife and start a family of his own.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he would do his best to find a good wife as soon as possible, and that he was confident that with her guidance and blessing, he would make her proud.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he had given any more thought to the matter of marriage, her voice barely above a whisper as she gazed at him with a mixture of hope and concern.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son reassured O-lan that he had indeed given the matter of marriage a great deal of thought, and he had already spoken to the village matchmaker, who was willing to help him find a suitable bride.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if he would be able to see to the matter of the matchmaker's fee, as she had heard it was a considerable sum.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would take care of the matchmaker's fee, but he insisted that it was not the time to be worrying about such things, and that O-lan's health was what mattered most.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad he would take care of the matchmaker's fee, but she knew that the cost of the wedding would be a burden on their family, and she hoped that the eldest son would be able to find a bride who was willing to work hard and bring prosperity to their household.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son assured O-lan that he would do his best to find a bride who would be a hard worker and bring prosperity to their household.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to it that the matchmaker's fee was paid, and that he would also make sure that the eldest son had a good harvest this year, so that he could marry well and bring prosperity to their family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad he had promised to take care of the matchmaker's fee, but she still worried about the family's future, especially with her own health failing.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not worry about the family's future, for he was a strong and capable man, and he would provide for them all, no matter what happened.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she had been watching the eldest son and thought he would be happy with anyone he chose, but perhaps it would be best to consider a bride from their own village, so that she could help with the household chores and learn the ways of the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son that she was glad he had found a suitable girl, but she still worried about the matchmaker's fee, and asked Wang Lung if he had made any arrangements to pay it.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if it would be acceptable to her if the eldest son were to marry someone from the neighboring village, where the family had connections and could rely on their support.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he was grateful for her concern and that he was confident that he would make the right choice for his future bride, and that he would not worry her with the details.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he had given any more thought to the matchmaker's fee, and how he planned to pay it

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he had already spoken to a few villagers and had a good idea of the matchmaker's fee, and that he would make arrangements to pay it as soon as possible.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
